subject: Reparametrization and PC-prior in latent model

messages.author: 828d260a55f62325
messages.subject: Reparametrization and PC-prior in latent model
parts:
Dear R-inla list

I have data which can be modelled as follows:


n = 100
prec.1=1
prec.2=5
nb = 4
nz1 = 5
nz2 = 10
Z1 = kronecker(diag(nz1),rep(1,20))
Z2 = matrix(runif(n*nz2), n, nz2)
b1 = rnorm(nz1,mean=0,sd=1/sqrt(prec.1))
b2 = rnorm(nz2,mean=0,sd=1/sqrt(prec.2))
beta = 5 + rnorm(nb)
X = matrix(runif(n*nb), n, nb)
X[,1] = 1 
eta = X %*% beta + Z1 %*% b1 + Z2 %*% b2
y = eta + rnorm(n, sd=0.01)

formula = y ~ -1 + X + f(id.z1, model="z", Z=Z1)+f(id.z2, model="z", Z=Z2)
result = inla(formula, data = list(y=y, id.z1 = 1:n,id.z2 = 1:n, X=X))

So it is a model with 2 random effects: one which is a sort of clustering random effect and another which is a more global random effect (for example a spatial effect although there is nothing spatial in the example above)
I am interested in a base model (or standard model) which is the model with only the cluster random effects, that is eta = X %*% beta + Z1 %*% b1. The model with two random effects is a generalization of the base model which I would like to use only if the base model does not fit well.

My question is if it is possible to fit my model in similar way as can be done with the  "bym2" model described in

http://inla.googlecode.com/hg-history/475192f4b6f3668d2637e54547517b3747082e16/r-inla.org/doc/latent/bym2.pdf

So basically v* would correspond to  Z1 %*% b1 and u* would correspond to  Z2 %*% b2.

If this is possible my other question is  if it is then possible to use this in combination with  the PC-priors of Simpson et al (2014)  more or less in the same way is done in the code shown in

http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/case-studies/Martins-etal-2014/bym/bym.R

Thanks in advance

Karim
